content: The camera permission flow is where indoor-scanning apps lose users, and mobile_scanner has specific documented traps. The maintainer's guidance (issue #1247, #509): on Android, requesting the permission triggers a lifecycle change when the popup opens, and denying it closes the popup and triggers didChangeAppLifecycleState again - so if that handler calls start() without checking permission state, the app enters an infinite permission-prompt loop. From v5.0.0 onward the guidance is not to call start() when the permission has been denied. A second trap (issue #847, #524): only controller.start() updates value.hasCameraPermission, so a user who permanently denied, then granted the permission in Settings and returned to the app gets stuck in the errorBuilder - the recommended fix is to consult permission_handler (Permission.camera.status.isGranted, shouldShowRequestRationale) in didChangeAppLifecycleState. Note also that on Android permission_handler's status never reports permanentlyDenied; you must call request() and branch on its result, and 'denied + shouldShowRequestRationale == false' means permanently denied. The errorBuilder should therefore offer two distinct paths: 'Grant permission' (re-request) and 'Open settings' (openAppSettings), decided by shouldShowRequestRationale. Other documented behaviour: MobileScannerErrorCode distinguishes permissionDenied, unsupported (no camera / desktop), controllerAlreadyInitialized, controllerUninitialized, controllerInitializing, controllerDisposed, controllerNotAttached - and start() must be awaited before the widget is built or the controllerNotAttached error is raised. Practical scanning guidance from an implementation writeup: restrict formats to [BarcodeFormat.qrCode] so detection is faster and false positives are rarer; use detectionSpeed.noDuplicates so a code left in view does not fire on every frame; and add a _handled flag because frames keep arriving while the async navigation call is in flight. Every scanned code should also be typeable by hand as a fallback - cameras break, lenses smudge, and not everyone grants camera access. Test on physical devices only (the iOS simulator has no camera), including an older cheap Android phone, in dim light with and without the torch, with glare, with small and damaged codes, with permission denied then granted from settings, and backgrounding the app mid-scan.
